sources.entry: OpenShot - Easy to use, quick to learn, and surprisingly powerful video editor.

summary.one_liner: OpenShot Video Editor is a free, open-source, cross-platform desktop video editor for Linux, Mac, and Windows, written in Python on top of libopenshot.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a desktop video editor with a multi-track timeline supporting unlimited tracks, clip trimming, cutting, scaling, rotation, and snapping. It offers curve-based keyframe animation, video transitions with real-time previews, and digital video effects such as brightness, gamma, hue, greyscale, and chroma key. Titles can be made from templates or created directly, including 3D animated titles and SVG-based vector titles and scrolling credits. It supports time-mapping and speed changes on clips, audio mixing, and frame-by-frame stepping, and can import and export EDL and XML. Media handling and rendering rely on FFmpeg, and experimental hardware encoding and decoding (VA-API, NVDEC, D3D9, D3D11, VTB) is listed.
use_cases: add titles and credits to a video
change clip speed or play backward
exchange timelines via EDL or XML
how_to_run: Download a pre-built installer from the OpenShot download page (Daily Builds for the latest experimental builds)
For a source build of libopenshot: cmake -B build -S . [options] && cmake --build build, then run with PYTHONPATH pointing to the bindings/python build folder
notable: Import and export of EDL and XML timelines
Experimental hardware encoding and decoding (VA-API, NVDEC, D3D9, D3D11, VTB)
Selectable Qt binding via OPENSHOT_QT_API environment variable
Distributed as pre-built installers and daily builds
caveats: Building from source requires separately built libopenshot and libopenshot-audio libraries plus FFmpeg and a Qt binding
README's install and build section is brief and points to external instructions for details
